CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is South Labuhanbatu Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regent is the Regent of South Labuhanbatu.
4. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion, whether direct or indirect, based on human differences on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that result in the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life, both individual and collective, in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life.
5. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering, whether physical, sexual, psychological, and/or domestic neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of a person's freedom unlawfully. 6. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a Child who is still in the womb.
7. Woman is a person who is female.
8. Violence against Women is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering of Women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or in private life.
9. Violence against Children is any act that results in or may result in suffering of Children physically, psychologically, sexually, neglect, exploitation, and other violence.
10. Victim is a Woman and Child who experiences violence and/or threat of violence.
11. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, police, prosecutor's office, court, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that Violence against Women will, is, or has occurred.
12. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from acts of Violence and discrimination.
13. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the Victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that Violence against the Victim will, is, or has occurred.
14. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to accompany Victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy, integrated for the strengthening and recovery of Violence Victims.
15. Gender is the difference in nature, role, function and status between Women and men which is not based on biological differences, but rather based on socio-cultural relations influenced by the broader structure of society.
16. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate Gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of policies, programs, and development activities in the region.
17. Office of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection, hereinafter abbreviated as Dinas PPPA, is the office that administers the affairs of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
18. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an integrated Service center in the effort to empower Women and Children established by the Regional Government with active Community participation which includes an information center, consultation center, complaint service, initial health care, counseling, legal assistance, repatriation and social reintegration, shelter/temporary safe house, and referral center.
19. Safe House is a shelter/temporary protection house for Victims, during the accompaniment process, for the safety and comfort of Victims from threats and dangers of perpetrators, and is only known to interested parties such as certain personnel at UPT P2TP2A for reasons of safety and security of Victims.
20. Standard Operating Procedure, hereinafter abbreviated as SOP, is the standard steps that must be taken in protecting Victims starting from complaints/identification, rehabilitation, health, Social Rehabilitation, advocacy to repatriation and social reintegration of witnesses and/or Victims.
21. Family is the smallest unit in Society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their Child, or father and his Child, or mother and her Child or Family by blood in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree and/or if any up to the fourth degree.
22. Household is husband, wife, and Child, people who have Family relations due to blood relations, marriage, breastfeeding, care, representation, and/or Household workers and reside in that Household.
23. Community is individuals, Families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.
24. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget, hereinafter abbreviated as APBD, is the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of South Labuhanbatu Regency.
25. Social Rehabilitation is a process of refunctionalization and development to enable a person to be able to carry out social functions properly in Community life.

Article 29

1. The regional apparatus in charge of Women and Children is obliged to formulate service policies regarding the protection of Women and Children from acts of Violence.
2. The formulation of service policies as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented with the mechanism of:
a. formulating case reporting policies related to Women and Children who are Victims of acts of Violence;
b. compiling reporting and referral mechanisms between regional apparatus organizations in charge of the protection of Women and Children against acts of Violence with related agencies and with P2TP2A; and
c. compiling a budget for implementing policies on the protection of Women and Children against acts of Violence.

Article 15

1. The Regional Government is obliged to:
a. implement policies for the protection of Women and Children from acts of Violence established by the government;
b. establish policies, programs, and activities for the protection of Women and Children from acts of Violence; and
c. cooperate with law enforcement apparatus, government apparatus, as well as educational institutions, health institutions, hospitals, and various NGOs concerned with Women and Children in the implementation of protection of Women and Children from acts of Violence.
2. The Regional Government is responsible for providing support for facilities and infrastructure for the implementation of protection of Women and Children from acts of Violence.
3. In order to carry out the obligations as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b, the Regional Government establishes action programs and activities for the protection of Women and Children in 1 (one) Regional Action Plan as a basis for regional apparatus in implementing protection of Women and Child Victims of Violence.
4. The Regional Action Plan as referred to in paragraph (3), is part of the Regional Medium-Term Development Plan (RPJMD).
5. The Regional Action Plan as referred to in paragraph (3), is further regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 14

The Regional Government is obliged and responsible for the implementation of protection of Women and Children from acts of Violence.

Article 31

1. Fulfillment of social welfare of Women and Children aims to prevent, reduce vulnerability risks and handle Victims of acts of Violence.
2. Fulfillment of social welfare of Women and Children as referred to in paragraph (1) is coordinated by the regional apparatus in charge of social affairs.

Article 17

The obligations of the Family and/or parents as referred to in Article 13 letters c and d have full responsibility to prevent all forms of Violence and protect Women and Children as Family members.

Article 48

1. The Regional Government may provide financial assistance to Community organizations, social organizations, or Community self-help institutions and universities that implement protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence.
2. Financial assistance as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be in accordance with the Regional financial capacity and implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 43

1. Community social institutions as referred to in Article 42 paragraph (2) letter d, in implementing the protection of Women and Children against acts of Violence must coordinate with P2TP2A.
2. The Regional Government encourages the business sector to participate in the protection of Women and Children against acts of Violence.
3. Participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may be in the form of:
a. socialization to employees within the company environment regarding the dangers of acts of Violence against Women and Children; and
b. assistance as a form of corporate social responsibility.

CHAPTER VIII

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 44

1. The Regional Government conducts guidance and supervision of the implementation of protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence.
2. Guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented periodically by the Regional Apparatus having authority over the empowerment of Women and Children against acts of Violence.
3. Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) includes:
a. guidelines and fulfillment standards;
b. technical guidance and training;
c. provision of facilities;
d. monitoring; and
e. evaluation.
4. Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted with the principles of:
a. professional;
b. transparent; and
c. accountable.

CHAPTER VII

COMMUNITY AND BUSINESS PARTICIPATION

Article 42

1. Every person may participate in providing protection for Women and Children from acts of Violence.
2. Participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may be carried out by:
a. reporting acts of Violence against Women and/or Children;
b. providing first aid to Victims;
c. independently socializing the rights of Women and Children; and/or
d. establishing independent Community social institutions.

Article 24

1. Assistance for Women and Children Victims of acts of Violence is carried out by persons and/or institutions cooperating with P2TP2A.
2. Assistance as referred to in paragraph (1), is conducted according to the SOP.
3. Further provisions regarding assistance as referred to in paragraph (2) are regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 45

Guidance and supervision as referred to in Article 44, shall be conducted in order to realize the objectives of implementing protection for Women and Children from acts of Violence in accordance with minimum Service standards established by laws and regulations.

Article 3

This Regional Regulation is intended to provide a legal basis for the Regional Government in providing protection for Women and Children from acts of Violence.

Article 11

Exploitation as referred to in Article 6 letter e is caused by:
a. acts that exploit economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the consent of the Victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or Services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial; and/or
c. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of the Victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or indecency.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is South Labuhanbatu Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regent is the Regent of South Labuhanbatu.
4. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion, whether direct or indirect, based on human differences on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that result in the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life, both individual and collective, in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life.
5. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering, whether physical, sexual, psychological, and/or domestic neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of a person's freedom unlawfully. 6. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a Child who is still in the womb.
7. Woman is a person who is female.
8. Violence against Women is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering of Women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or in private life.
9. Violence against Children is any act that results in or may result in suffering of Children physically, psychologically, sexually, neglect, exploitation, and other violence.
10. Victim is a Woman and Child who experiences violence and/or threat of violence.
11. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, police, prosecutor's office, court, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that Violence against Women will, is, or has occurred.
12. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from acts of Violence and discrimination.
13. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the Victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that Violence against the Victim will, is, or has occurred.
14. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to accompany Victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy, integrated for the strengthening and recovery of Violence Victims.
15. Gender is the difference in nature, role, function and status between Women and men which is not based on biological differences, but rather based on socio-cultural relations influenced by the broader structure of society.
16. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate Gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of policies, programs, and development activities in the region.
17. Office of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection, hereinafter abbreviated as Dinas PPPA, is the office that administers the affairs of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
18. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an integrated Service center in the effort to empower Women and Children established by the Regional Government with active Community participation which includes an information center, consultation center, complaint service, initial health care, counseling, legal assistance, repatriation and social reintegration, shelter/temporary safe house, and referral center.
19. Safe House is a shelter/temporary protection house for Victims, during the accompaniment process, for the safety and comfort of Victims from threats and dangers of perpetrators, and is only known to interested parties such as certain personnel at UPT P2TP2A for reasons of safety and security of Victims.
20. Standard Operating Procedure, hereinafter abbreviated as SOP, is the standard steps that must be taken in protecting Victims starting from complaints/identification, rehabilitation, health, Social Rehabilitation, advocacy to repatriation and social reintegration of witnesses and/or Victims.
21. Family is the smallest unit in Society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their Child, or father and his Child, or mother and her Child or Family by blood in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree and/or if any up to the fourth degree.
22. Household is husband, wife, and Child, people who have Family relations due to blood relations, marriage, breastfeeding, care, representation, and/or Household workers and reside in that Household.
23. Community is individuals, Families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.
24. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget, hereinafter abbreviated as APBD, is the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of South Labuhanbatu Regency.
25. Social Rehabilitation is a process of refunctionalization and development to enable a person to be able to carry out social functions properly in Community life.

Article 24

1. Assistance for Women and Children Victims of acts of Violence is carried out by persons and/or institutions cooperating with P2TP2A.
2. Assistance as referred to in paragraph (1), is conducted according to the SOP.
3. Further provisions regarding assistance as referred to in paragraph (2) are regulated by Regent Regulation.

Part Four

Assistance Mechanism by Persons and/or Institutions Cooperating with P2TP2A

Part One

General

Article 15

1. The Regional Government is obliged to:
a. implement policies for the protection of Women and Children from acts of Violence established by the government;
b. establish policies, programs, and activities for the protection of Women and Children from acts of Violence; and
c. cooperate with law enforcement apparatus, government apparatus, as well as educational institutions, health institutions, hospitals, and various NGOs concerned with Women and Children in the implementation of protection of Women and Children from acts of Violence.
2. The Regional Government is responsible for providing support for facilities and infrastructure for the implementation of protection of Women and Children from acts of Violence.
3. In order to carry out the obligations as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b, the Regional Government establishes action programs and activities for the protection of Women and Children in 1 (one) Regional Action Plan as a basis for regional apparatus in implementing protection of Women and Child Victims of Violence.
4. The Regional Action Plan as referred to in paragraph (3), is part of the Regional Medium-Term Development Plan (RPJMD).
5. The Regional Action Plan as referred to in paragraph (3), is further regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 29

1. The regional apparatus in charge of Women and Children is obliged to formulate service policies regarding the protection of Women and Children from acts of Violence.
2. The formulation of service policies as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented with the mechanism of:
a. formulating case reporting policies related to Women and Children who are Victims of acts of Violence;
b. compiling reporting and referral mechanisms between regional apparatus organizations in charge of the protection of Women and Children against acts of Violence with related agencies and with P2TP2A; and
c. compiling a budget for implementing policies on the protection of Women and Children against acts of Violence.

CHAPTER VIII

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 44

1. The Regional Government conducts guidance and supervision of the implementation of protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence.
2. Guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented periodically by the Regional Apparatus having authority over the empowerment of Women and Children against acts of Violence.

a. guidelines and fulfillment standards;
b. technical guidance and training;
c. provision of facilities;
d. monitoring; and
e. evaluation.

a. professional;
b. transparent; and
c. accountable.

b. assistance as a form of corporate social responsibility.

Article 18

In order to provide Services and protection to Women and Children from acts of Violence, the Regional Government establishes P2TP2A.

Article 2

Point a What is meant by "the principle of respect for human rights" is that the implementation of protection for Women and Children victims of violence is to ensure the fulfillment of the rights of victims of violence as a manifestation of respect for human rights.

Point b What is meant by "the right to life, survival, and development" are the rights as regulated in the provisions of the 1945 Constitution.

Point c What is meant by "Non-discriminatory" is an attitude and treatment toward victims without making distinctions based on age, gender, race, ethnicity, religion and between groups.

Point d What is meant by the principle of the best interests of the Child is that in all actions concerning Children carried out by the government, society, legislative bodies, and judicial bodies, the best interests of the child must be the primary consideration.

Point e What is meant by "the principle of Gender equality and justice" is a process of equality and conditions for men and Women to obtain equal opportunities and rights as human beings, so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, defense and national security activities and equality in enjoying the results of such development.

Point f What is meant by "the principle of protection of victims' rights" is protection of personal self, Family, honor, dignity, and property under their control, a sense of security and protection from threats of fear, freedom from torture or treatment that degrades human dignity.

I. GENERAL

Violence against Women and Children constitutes a violation of Human Rights and therefore their dignity and honor must be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination. Based on empirical evidence, it is revealed that Women and Children are groups that frequently become victims of violence. Many factors cause violence against Women and Children, including the patriarchal cultural factor that still occurs widely in society which views Women as lower than men. In addition, incorrect perceptions about violence against Women and Children are also still commonly found, which consider violence as normal and as the right of the perpetrator. Violence against Women and Children can be seen from the type, perpetrator, location of incident, time, age and consequences of the act of violence. Violence against Women and Children as mentioned above is general in nature and has no relevance to the type of education, occupation and income, social status, religion and belief, nationality, ethnicity and race attached to men and Women. This means that in all types of social strata, violence against Women and Children can and continues to occur as long as the imbalance in the relationship between men and Women is still believed and manifested in social life. In order to prevent and overcome Violence against Women and Children in South Labuhanbatu Regency so that they are protected from Violence, threats of Violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, a legal umbrella is needed in the form of regulations in the Region.

So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of Women and Children from acts of Violence have not yet regulated protection efforts in the Region, so institutional and regulatory support is needed to ensure its implementation.

The formulation of this Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence is intended to provide a legal basis for the Regional Government in providing protection for Women and Children in the South Labuhanbatu Regency area.

Article 2

Point a What is meant by "the principle of respect for human rights" is that the implementation of protection for Women and Children victims of violence is to ensure the fulfillment of the rights of victims of violence as a manifestation of respect for human rights.

Point b What is meant by "the right to life, survival, and development" are the rights as regulated in the provisions of the 1945 Constitution.

Point c What is meant by "Non-discriminatory" is an attitude and treatment toward victims without making distinctions based on age, gender, race, ethnicity, religion and between groups.

Point d What is meant by the principle of the best interests of the Child is that in all actions concerning Children carried out by the government, society, legislative bodies, and judicial bodies, the best interests of the child must be the primary consideration.

Part Four

I. GENERAL

Violence against Women and Children constitutes a violation of Human Rights and therefore their dignity and honor must be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination. Based on empirical evidence, it is revealed that Women and Children are groups that frequently become victims of violence. Many factors cause violence against Women and Children, including the patriarchal cultural factor that still occurs widely in society which views Women as lower than men. In addition, incorrect perceptions about violence against Women and Children are also still commonly found, which consider violence as normal and as the right of the perpetrator. Violence against Women and Children can be seen from the type, perpetrator, location of incident, time, age and consequences of the act of violence. Violence against Women and Children as mentioned above is general in nature and has no relevance to the type of education, occupation and income, social status, religion and belief, nationality, ethnicity and race attached to men and Women. This means that in all types of social strata, violence against Women and Children can and continues to occur as long as the imbalance in the relationship between men and Women is still believed and manifested in social life. In order to prevent and overcome Violence against Women and Children in South Labuhanbatu Regency so that they are protected from Violence, threats of Violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, a legal umbrella is needed in the form of regulations in the Region.

So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of Women and Children from acts of Violence have not yet regulated protection efforts in the Region, so institutional and regulatory support is needed to ensure its implementation.

The formulation of this Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence is intended to provide a legal basis for the Regional Government in providing protection for Women and Children in the South Labuhanbatu Regency area.

I. GENERAL

Violence against Women and Children constitutes a violation of Human Rights and therefore their dignity and honor must be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination. Based on empirical evidence, it is revealed that Women and Children are groups that frequently become victims of violence. Many factors cause violence against Women and Children, including the patriarchal cultural factor that still occurs widely in society which views Women as lower than men. In addition, incorrect perceptions about violence against Women and Children are also still commonly found, which consider violence as normal and as the right of the perpetrator. Violence against Women and Children can be seen from the type, perpetrator, location of incident, time, age and consequences of the act of violence. Violence against Women and Children as mentioned above is general in nature and has no relevance to the type of education, occupation and income, social status, religion and belief, nationality, ethnicity and race attached to men and Women. This means that in all types of social strata, violence against Women and Children can and continues to occur as long as the imbalance in the relationship between men and Women is still believed and manifested in social life. In order to prevent and overcome Violence against Women and Children in South Labuhanbatu Regency so that they are protected from Violence, threats of Violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, a legal umbrella is needed in the form of regulations in the Region.

So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of Women and Children from acts of Violence have not yet regulated protection efforts in the Region, so institutional and regulatory support is needed to ensure its implementation.

I. GENERAL

Violence against Women and Children constitutes a violation of Human Rights and therefore their dignity and honor must be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination. Based on empirical evidence, it is revealed that Women and Children are groups that frequently become victims of violence. Many factors cause violence against Women and Children, including the patriarchal cultural factor that still occurs widely in society which views Women as lower than men. In addition, incorrect perceptions about violence against Women and Children are also still commonly found, which consider violence as normal and as the right of the perpetrator. Violence against Women and Children can be seen from the type, perpetrator, location of incident, time, age and consequences of the act of violence. Violence against Women and Children as mentioned above is general in nature and has no relevance to the type of education, occupation and income, social status, religion and belief, nationality, ethnicity and race attached to men and Women. This means that in all types of social strata, violence against Women and Children can and continues to occur as long as the imbalance in the relationship between men and Women is still believed and manifested in social life. In order to prevent and overcome Violence against Women and Children in South Labuhanbatu Regency so that they are protected from Violence, threats of Violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, a legal umbrella is needed in the form of regulations in the Region.

So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of Women and Children from acts of Violence have not yet regulated protection efforts in the Region, so institutional and regulatory support is needed to ensure its implementation.

The formulation of this Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence is intended to provide a legal basis for the Regional Government in providing protection for Women and Children in the South Labuhanbatu Regency area.

CHAPTER V

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Violence against Women and Children constitutes a violation of Human Rights and therefore their dignity and honor must be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination. Based on empirical evidence, it is revealed that Women and Children are groups that frequently become victims of violence. Many factors cause violence against Women and Children, including the patriarchal cultural factor that still occurs widely in society which views Women as lower than men. In addition, incorrect perceptions about violence against Women and Children are also still commonly found, which consider violence as normal and as the right of the perpetrator. Violence against Women and Children can be seen from the type, perpetrator, location of incident, time, age and consequences of the act of violence. Violence against Women and Children as mentioned above is general in nature and has no relevance to the type of education, occupation and income, social status, religion and belief, nationality, ethnicity and race attached to men and Women. This means that in all types of social strata, violence against Women and Children can and continues to occur as long as the imbalance in the relationship between men and Women is still believed and manifested in social life. In order to prevent and overcome Violence against Women and Children in South Labuhanbatu Regency so that they are protected from Violence, threats of Violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, a legal umbrella is needed in the form of regulations in the Region.

So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of Women and Children from acts of Violence have not yet regulated protection efforts in the Region, so institutional and regulatory support is needed to ensure its implementation.

The formulation of this Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence is intended to provide a legal basis for the Regional Government in providing protection for Women and Children in the South Labuhanbatu Regency area.

I. GENERAL

Violence against Women and Children constitutes a violation of Human Rights and therefore their dignity and honor must be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination. Based on empirical evidence, it is revealed that Women and Children are groups that frequently become victims of violence. Many factors cause violence against Women and Children, including the patriarchal cultural factor that still occurs widely in society which views Women as lower than men. In addition, incorrect perceptions about violence against Women and Children are also still commonly found, which consider violence as normal and as the right of the perpetrator. Violence against Women and Children can be seen from the type, perpetrator, location of incident, time, age and consequences of the act of violence. Violence against Women and Children as mentioned above is general in nature and has no relevance to the type of education, occupation and income, social status, religion and belief, nationality, ethnicity and race attached to men and Women. This means that in all types of social strata, violence against Women and Children can and continues to occur as long as the imbalance in the relationship between men and Women is still believed and manifested in social life. In order to prevent and overcome Violence against Women and Children in South Labuhanbatu Regency so that they are protected from Violence, threats of Violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, a legal umbrella is needed in the form of regulations in the Region.

So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of Women and Children from acts of Violence have not yet regulated protection efforts in the Region, so institutional and regulatory support is needed to ensure its implementation.

The formulation of this Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence is intended to provide a legal basis for the Regional Government in providing protection for Women and Children in the South Labuhanbatu Regency area.

Part One

General

I. GENERAL

Violence against Women and Children constitutes a violation of Human Rights and therefore their dignity and honor must be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination. Based on empirical evidence, it is revealed that Women and Children are groups that frequently become victims of violence. Many factors cause violence against Women and Children, including the patriarchal cultural factor that still occurs widely in society which views Women as lower than men. In addition, incorrect perceptions about violence against Women and Children are also still commonly found, which consider violence as normal and as the right of the perpetrator. Violence against Women and Children can be seen from the type, perpetrator, location of incident, time, age and consequences of the act of violence. Violence against Women and Children as mentioned above is general in nature and has no relevance to the type of education, occupation and income, social status, religion and belief, nationality, ethnicity and race attached to men and Women. This means that in all types of social strata, violence against Women and Children can and continues to occur as long as the imbalance in the relationship between men and Women is still believed and manifested in social life. In order to prevent and overcome Violence against Women and Children in South Labuhanbatu Regency so that they are protected from Violence, threats of Violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, a legal umbrella is needed in the form of regulations in the Region.

So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of Women and Children from acts of Violence have not yet regulated protection efforts in the Region, so institutional and regulatory support is needed to ensure its implementation.

The formulation of this Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence is intended to provide a legal basis for the Regional Government in providing protection for Women and Children in the South Labuhanbatu Regency area.

I. GENERAL

Violence against Women and Children constitutes a violation of Human Rights and therefore their dignity and honor must be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination. Based on empirical evidence, it is revealed that Women and Children are groups that frequently become victims of violence. Many factors cause violence against Women and Children, including the patriarchal cultural factor that still occurs widely in society which views Women as lower than men. In addition, incorrect perceptions about violence against Women and Children are also still commonly found, which consider violence as normal and as the right of the perpetrator. Violence against Women and Children can be seen from the type, perpetrator, location of incident, time, age and consequences of the act of violence. Violence against Women and Children as mentioned above is general in nature and has no relevance to the type of education, occupation and income, social status, religion and belief, nationality, ethnicity and race attached to men and Women. This means that in all types of social strata, violence against Women and Children can and continues to occur as long as the imbalance in the relationship between men and Women is still believed and manifested in social life. In order to prevent and overcome Violence against Women and Children in South Labuhanbatu Regency so that they are protected from Violence, threats of Violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, a legal umbrella is needed in the form of regulations in the Region.

So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of Women and Children from acts of Violence have not yet regulated protection efforts in the Region, so institutional and regulatory support is needed to ensure its implementation.

The formulation of this Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence is intended to provide a legal basis for the Regional Government in providing protection for Women and Children in the South Labuhanbatu Regency area.

Article 30

1. Regional Government, Community and private sector provide facilities and infrastructure in the protection of Women and Children, among others providing breastfeeding places for Children, child-friendly play areas, recreation and creation places, Safe Houses, and establishing Integrated Service Centers for the Protection of Women and Children.
2. Facilities and infrastructure as referred to in paragraph (1) must meet the following criteria:
a. ensure safety, comfort and health;
b. motivate Children's creativity; and
c. contain educational elements.
3. Provision of facilities and infrastructure as referred to in paragraph (2) for the fulfillment of minimum Service standards.
4. Provision of facilities and infrastructure by the Regional Government is carried out in stages adjusted to the Regional financial capacity.

I. GENERAL

Violence against Women and Children constitutes a violation of Human Rights and therefore their dignity and honor must be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination. Based on empirical evidence, it is revealed that Women and Children are groups that frequently become victims of violence. Many factors cause violence against Women and Children, including the patriarchal cultural factor that still occurs widely in society which views Women as lower than men. In addition, incorrect perceptions about violence against Women and Children are also still commonly found, which consider violence as normal and as the right of the perpetrator. Violence against Women and Children can be seen from the type, perpetrator, location of incident, time, age and consequences of the act of violence. Violence against Women and Children as mentioned above is general in nature and has no relevance to the type of education, occupation and income, social status, religion and belief, nationality, ethnicity and race attached to men and Women. This means that in all types of social strata, violence against Women and Children can and continues to occur as long as the imbalance in the relationship between men and Women is still believed and manifested in social life. In order to prevent and overcome Violence against Women and Children in South Labuhanbatu Regency so that they are protected from Violence, threats of Violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, a legal umbrella is needed in the form of regulations in the Region.

So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of Women and Children from acts of Violence have not yet regulated protection efforts in the Region, so institutional and regulatory support is needed to ensure its implementation.

The formulation of this Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence is intended to provide a legal basis for the Regional Government in providing protection for Women and Children in the South Labuhanbatu Regency area.

CHAPTER V

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE

Article 2

Point a What is meant by "the principle of respect for human rights" is that the implementation of protection for Women and Children victims of violence is to ensure the fulfillment of the rights of victims of violence as a manifestation of respect for human rights.

Point b What is meant by "the right to life, survival, and development" are the rights as regulated in the provisions of the 1945 Constitution.

Point c What is meant by "Non-discriminatory" is an attitude and treatment toward victims without making distinctions based on age, gender, race, ethnicity, religion and between groups.

Point d What is meant by the principle of the best interests of the Child is that in all actions concerning Children carried out by the government, society, legislative bodies, and judicial bodies, the best interests of the child must be the primary consideration.

Point e What is meant by "the principle of Gender equality and justice" is a process of equality and conditions for men and Women to obtain equal opportunities and rights as human beings, so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, defense and national security activities and equality in enjoying the results of such development.

Point f What is meant by "the principle of protection of victims' rights" is protection of personal self, Family, honor, dignity, and property under their control, a sense of security and protection from threats of fear, freedom from torture or treatment that degrades human dignity.

Article 48

1. The Regional Government may provide financial assistance to Community organizations, social organizations, or Community self-help institutions and universities that implement protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence.
2. Financial assistance as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be in accordance with the Regional financial capacity and implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 29

1. The regional apparatus in charge of Women and Children is obliged to formulate service policies regarding the protection of Women and Children from acts of Violence.

a. formulating case reporting policies related to Women and Children who are Victims of acts of Violence;
b. compiling reporting and referral mechanisms between regional apparatus organizations in charge of the protection of Women and Children against acts of Violence with related agencies and with P2TP2A; and
c. compiling a budget for implementing policies on the protection of Women and Children against acts of Violence.

Article 15

1. The Regional Government is obliged to:
a. implement policies for the protection of Women and Children from acts of Violence established by the government;
b. establish policies, programs, and activities for the protection of Women and Children from acts of Violence; and
c. cooperate with law enforcement apparatus, government apparatus, as well as educational institutions, health institutions, hospitals, and various NGOs concerned with Women and Children in the implementation of protection of Women and Children from acts of Violence.
2. The Regional Government is responsible for providing support for facilities and infrastructure for the implementation of protection of Women and Children from acts of Violence.
3. In order to carry out the obligations as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b, the Regional Government establishes action programs and activities for the protection of Women and Children in 1 (one) Regional Action Plan as a basis for regional apparatus in implementing protection of Women and Child Victims of Violence.
4. The Regional Action Plan as referred to in paragraph (3), is part of the Regional Medium-Term Development Plan (RPJMD).
5. The Regional Action Plan as referred to in paragraph (3), is further regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 31

1. Fulfillment of social welfare of Women and Children aims to prevent, reduce vulnerability risks and handle Victims of acts of Violence.
2. Fulfillment of social welfare of Women and Children as referred to in paragraph (1) is coordinated by the regional apparatus in charge of social affairs.

Article 30

1. Regional Government, Community and private sector provide facilities and infrastructure in the protection of Women and Children, among others providing breastfeeding places for Children, child-friendly play areas, recreation and creation places, Safe Houses, and establishing Integrated Service Centers for the Protection of Women and Children.
2. Facilities and infrastructure as referred to in paragraph (1) must meet the following criteria:
a. ensure safety, comfort and health;
b. motivate Children's creativity; and
c. contain educational elements.
3. Provision of facilities and infrastructure as referred to in paragraph (2) for the fulfillment of minimum Service standards.
4. Provision of facilities and infrastructure by the Regional Government is carried out in stages adjusted to the Regional financial capacity.

CHAPTER VIII

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 44

1. The Regional Government conducts guidance and supervision of the implementation of protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence.
2. Guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented periodically by the Regional Apparatus having authority over the empowerment of Women and Children against acts of Violence.
3. Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) includes:
a. guidelines and fulfillment standards;
b. technical guidance and training;
c. provision of facilities;
d. monitoring; and
e. evaluation.
4. Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted with the principles of:
a. professional;
b. transparent; and
c. accountable.

Article 35

1. The Regional Government may establish a Gender Mainstreaming Working Group.

4. Each member of the Working Group as referred to in paragraph (2) may appoint a Gender Mainstreaming Focal Point.

I. GENERAL

Violence against Women and Children constitutes a violation of Human Rights and therefore their dignity and honor must be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination. Based on empirical evidence, it is revealed that Women and Children are groups that frequently become victims of violence. Many factors cause violence against Women and Children, including the patriarchal cultural factor that still occurs widely in society which views Women as lower than men. In addition, incorrect perceptions about violence against Women and Children are also still commonly found, which consider violence as normal and as the right of the perpetrator. Violence against Women and Children can be seen from the type, perpetrator, location of incident, time, age and consequences of the act of violence. Violence against Women and Children as mentioned above is general in nature and has no relevance to the type of education, occupation and income, social status, religion and belief, nationality, ethnicity and race attached to men and Women. This means that in all types of social strata, violence against Women and Children can and continues to occur as long as the imbalance in the relationship between men and Women is still believed and manifested in social life. In order to prevent and overcome Violence against Women and Children in South Labuhanbatu Regency so that they are protected from Violence, threats of Violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, a legal umbrella is needed in the form of regulations in the Region.

So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of Women and Children from acts of Violence have not yet regulated protection efforts in the Region, so institutional and regulatory support is needed to ensure its implementation.

The formulation of this Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence is intended to provide a legal basis for the Regional Government in providing protection for Women and Children in the South Labuhanbatu Regency area.

Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion, whether direct or indirect, based on human differences on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that result in the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life, both individual and collective, in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life.
5. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering, whether physical, sexual, psychological, and/or domestic neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of a person's freedom unlawfully. 6. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a Child who is still in the womb.
7. Woman is a person who is female.

I. GENERAL

Violence against Women and Children constitutes a violation of Human Rights and therefore their dignity and honor must be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination. GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is South Labuhanbatu Regency.

3. Regent is the Regent of South Labuhanbatu.
4. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion, whether direct or indirect, based on human differences on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that result in the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life, both individual and collective, in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life.
5. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering, whether physical, sexual, psychological, and/or domestic neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of a person's freedom unlawfully. 6. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a Child who is still in the womb.
7. Woman is a person who is female.
8. Violence against Women is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering of Women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or in private life.
9. Violence against Children is any act that results in or may result in suffering of Children physically, psychologically, sexually, neglect, exploitation, and other violence.
10. Victim is a Woman and Child who experiences violence and/or threat of violence.
11. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, police, prosecutor's office, court, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that Violence against Women will, is, or has occurred.
12. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from acts of Violence and discrimination.
13. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the Victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that Violence against the Victim will, is, or has occurred.
14. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to accompany Victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy, integrated for the strengthening and recovery of Violence Victims.
15. Gender is the difference in nature, role, function and status between Women and men which is not based on biological differences, but rather based on socio-cultural relations influenced by the broader structure of society.
16. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate Gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of policies, programs, and development activities in the region.
17. Office of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection, hereinafter abbreviated as Dinas PPPA, is the office that administers the affairs of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
18. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an integrated Service center in the effort to empower Women and Children established by the Regional Government with active Community participation which includes an information center, consultation center, complaint service, initial health care, counseling, legal assistance, repatriation and social reintegration, shelter/temporary safe house, and referral center.
19. Safe House is a shelter/temporary protection house for Victims, during the accompaniment process, for the safety and comfort of Victims from threats and dangers of perpetrators, and is only known to interested parties such as certain personnel at UPT P2TP2A for reasons of safety and security of Victims.
20. Standard Operating Procedure, hereinafter abbreviated as SOP, is the standard steps that must be taken in protecting Victims starting from complaints/identification, rehabilitation, health, Social Rehabilitation, advocacy to repatriation and social reintegration of witnesses and/or Victims.
21. Family is the smallest unit in Society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their Child, or father and his Child, or mother and her Child or Family by blood in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree and/or if any up to the fourth degree.

23. Community is individuals, Families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.
24. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget, hereinafter abbreviated as APBD, is the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of South Labuhanbatu Regency.

Article 45

Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an integrated Service center in the effort to empower Women and Children established by the Regional Government with active Community participation which includes an information center, consultation center, complaint service, initial health care, counseling, legal assistance, repatriation and social reintegration, shelter/temporary safe house, and referral center.
19. Safe House is a shelter/temporary protection house for Victims, during the accompaniment process, for the safety and comfort of Victims from threats and dangers of perpetrators, and is only known to interested parties such as certain personnel at UPT P2TP2A for reasons of safety and security of Victims.
20. Standard Operating Procedure, hereinafter abbreviated as SOP, is the standard steps that must be taken in protecting Victims starting from complaints/identification, rehabilitation, health, Social Rehabilitation, advocacy to repatriation and social reintegration of witnesses and/or Victims.
21. Family is the smallest unit in Society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their Child, or father and his Child, or mother and her Child or Family by blood in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree and/or if any up to the fourth degree.
22. Household is husband, wife, and Child, people who have Family relations due to blood relations, marriage, breastfeeding, care, representation, and/or Household workers and reside in that Household.
23. Community is individuals, Families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.
24. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget, hereinafter abbreviated as APBD, is the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of South Labuhanbatu Regency.
25. Social Rehabilitation is a process of refunctionalization and development to enable a person to be able to carry out social functions properly in Community life.

Article 30

1. Regional Government, Community and private sector provide facilities and infrastructure in the protection of Women and Children, among others providing breastfeeding places for Children, child-friendly play areas, recreation and creation places, Safe Houses, and establishing Integrated Service Centers for the Protection of Women and Children.
2. Facilities and infrastructure as referred to in paragraph (1) must meet the following criteria:
a. ensure safety, comfort and health;
b. motivate Children's creativity; and
c. contain educational elements.
3. Provision of facilities and infrastructure as referred to in paragraph (2) for the fulfillment of minimum Service standards.
4. Provision of facilities and infrastructure by the Regional Government is carried out in stages adjusted to the Regional financial capacity.

Article 34

1. Every regional apparatus is obliged to conduct Gender responsive budgeting planning.
2. Gender responsive budgeting planning as referred to in paragraph (1) is coordinated by the regional apparatus in the field of Women and Children.

Article 29

1. The regional apparatus in charge of Women and Children is obliged to formulate service policies regarding the protection of Women and Children from acts of Violence.
2. The formulation of service policies as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented with the mechanism of:
a. formulating case reporting policies related to Women and Children who are Victims of acts of Violence;
b. compiling reporting and referral mechanisms between regional apparatus organizations in charge of the protection of Women and Children against acts of Violence with related agencies and with P2TP2A; and
c. compiling a budget for implementing policies on the protection of Women and Children against acts of Violence.

5. The Regional Action Plan as referred to in paragraph (3), is further regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 37

1. Social behavior change is carried out with the aim of changing ways of thinking, attitudes and actions in accordance with parenting and education patterns that protect Children.
2. Behavior change is intended to change policies, programs and budget allocations along with their action plans to change the social behavior of individuals, groups, government and non-government institutions to implement Child protection.
3. The Regional apparatus authorized to implement behavior change as regulated in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) are Regional Apparatus in charge of social affairs, religion, health, education, Community empowerment, population, manpower, information and communication as well as Child protection under the coordination of the Regional Apparatus Organization in charge of the protection of Women and Children.

REPORTING

Article 46

1. The Regional Apparatus in charge of the empowerment of Women and Children from acts of Violence shall report the implementation of protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence to the Regent.
2. Reporting as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be submitted in writing, including:
